classification.difficultyReason: The student must recognise the translated circle from its parametric form, locate the endpoints relative to its centre, select the shorter quarter-circle arc, and calculate its length. These are linked familiar procedures without a supplied diagram.

content.prompt:
A function is defined parametrically by
$$x(t)=5\cos(2t)+1,\qquad y(t)=5\sin(2t)-1.$$
If $A(6,-1)$ and $B(1,4)$ are two points that lie on the function, then find the shortest distance along the graph from $A$ to $B$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\cos(2t)&=\frac{x-1}{5}\\\sin(2t)&=\frac{y+1}{5}\end{aligned}$$
Using $\cos^2(2t)+\sin^2(2t)=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{x-1}{5}\right)^2+\left(\frac{y+1}{5}\right)^2&=1\\(x-1)^2+(y+1)^2&=25\end{aligned}$$
The circle has centre $(1,-1)$ and radius $5$. $A$ and $B$ are its rightmost and topmost points, so the shortest arc between them is a quarter of the circle.
$$\begin{aligned}d&=\frac{2\pi\times5}{4}\\d&=\frac{5\pi}{2}\text{ units}\end{aligned}$$
